title: Top 3 Products per Category by Price
description:
Return the **top 3 most expensive products** within each category. If a category has fewer than 3 products, return all of them.

**Table: products**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| category | VARCHAR |
| price | DECIMAL |
| stock_quantity | INT |

Output columns: `category`, `name`, `price`. Order by `category`, `price` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, stock_quantity INT); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Laptop','Electronics',999.99,10),(2,'Phone','Electronics',699.99,25),(3,'Monitor','Electronics',349.99,15),(4,'Keyboard','Electronics',79.99,50),(5,'Desk','Furniture',299.99,5),(6,'Chair','Furniture',149.99,8),(7,'Stool','Furniture',89.99,12),(8,'Shelf','Furniture',59.99,20);
solution_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT name, category, price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rn FROM products) SELECT category, name, price FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 3 ORDER BY category, price DESC

test_cases.description: Top 3 per category: Electronics (Laptop, Phone, Monitor); Furniture (Desk, Chair, Stool)

hints: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) assigns 1 to the most expensive per category.
Filter WHERE rn <= 3 to keep only the top 3.
explanation: This is the classic 'top-N per group' pattern. ROW_NUMBER resets per category due to PARTITION BY. Keyboard (79.99) gets rn=4 in Electronics and is excluded. Shelf (59.99) gets rn=4 in Furniture and is excluded.
